lead.tldr: Coordinated DeFi rescue pledges 30,000 ETH, highlighting systemic risk but also strong community liquidity response • Justin Sun’s $20 million USDT injection into Aave may accelerate protocol expansion onto Tron’s growing DeFi ecosystem • Strategy’s $255 million BTC buy pushes treasury toward 1 million‑BTC goal, reinforcing institutional Bitcoin demand • DTCC clearance and NYSE on‑chain platform signal imminent wave of regulated tokenized securities for institutional investors • Israel’s approval of a shekel‑pegged stablecoin creates a regional fiat‑backed crypto model, likely spurring local adoption • Surge to 135 crypto kidnapping cases in France underscores rising physical‑coercion threats, prompting tighter security for high‑value holders

intro: Dear Founders, Investors, and Friends, DeFi projects rallied with a 30,000 ETH rescue while Strategy added $255 M of Bitcoin to its treasury, and Wall Street’s on‑chain tokenization push gained SEC clearance. Meanwhile, Israel approved a shekel‑pegged stablecoin and Tennessee moved to ban crypto kiosks, underscoring regulatory divergence.

top_signals.title: Ethereum Backers Commit 30,000 ETH to rsETH Recovery After Exploit
top_signals.summary: An exploit on April 18 drained roughly 116,500 rsETH, valued at about $290 million, from a LayerZero‑based bridge operated by Kelp DAO, creating up to $200 million of bad debt on Aave. In response, a coalition of DeFi projects known as DeFi United, including Lido, EtherFi, Ethena, Mantle, Frax and others, pledged 30,000 ETH to support the recovery of the compromised rsETH. Circle’s venture arm also purchased AAVE tokens to help stabilize the broader ecosystem after the incident. The coordinated capital injection aims to protect Ethereum‑based liquidity providers and mitigate systemic risk across interconnected DeFi protocols.

top_signals.title: Justin Sun announces $20m boost for Aave as he calls on lender to expand to his blockchain
top_signals.summary: Justin Sun has pledged a $20 million USDT liquidity injection to Aave’s Core V3 market. He simultaneously urged the lender to launch on the Tron blockchain. Tron, the fifth‑largest DeFi blockchain, holds about $5.3 billion in deposits and is actively courting high‑value protocols. The move follows a large hack of Aave earlier this year and underscores the importance of bolstering liquidity and expanding cross‑chain access for institutional participants.

top_signals.title: Strategy (MSTR) adds $255 million more bitcoin to its treasury which now holds 818,334
top_signals.summary: MicroStrategy (MSTR) purchased 3,273 Bitcoin for roughly $255 million, adding to its corporate treasury. The acquisition raises its total holdings to 818,334 Bitcoin, valued at about $61.8 billion at current market prices. This purchase aligns with the company’s stated aim of reaching a 1 million‑Bitcoin target and signals continued institutional confidence in Bitcoin.

top_signals.title: Why Wall Street is moving onchain - a16z crypto
top_signals.summary: Wall Street institutions are moving to on‑chain infrastructure, highlighted by the DTCC obtaining SEC clearance to tokenize assets. The NYSE has introduced a 24/7 on‑chain trading platform for equities and ETFs. The transition is described as the most significant upgrade to capital‑market infrastructure since electronic trading, offering faster settlement, fractional ownership and broader participation.

top_signals.title: Israeli Regulators Approve Shekel-Pegged Stablecoin
top_signals.summary: Israeli financial regulators have approved a stablecoin that is pegged to the Israeli shekel. The approval marks the first official endorsement of a fiat‑backed crypto token in Israel and signals regulatory clarity for digital asset projects. Institutional investors can view the development as a catalyst for increased crypto adoption and the launch of related financial services within the Israeli market.

top_signals.title: French police record 135 crypto kidnapping cases since 2023 as crime wave swells
top_signals.summary: French police have recorded 135 crypto‑related kidnapping cases since 2023, indicating a rapid increase in this type of crime. The incidents typically involve the extortion of Bitcoin and other altcoins, with perpetrators often coordinating the attacks through the Telegram messaging platform. Law‑enforcement actions have resulted in a series of arrests and the seizure of assets valued at several hundred thousand dollars. The trend underscores heightened operational risk for institutional investors with exposure to digital assets and highlights the need for robust security and compliance measures.

top_signals.title: Tennessee Crypto Kiosk Ban Set to Go into Effect July 1
top_signals.summary: Tennessee will prohibit the operation of crypto kiosks and ATMs beginning July 1. The statewide ban covers more than 570 devices, including those run by Bitcoin Depot and CoinFlip. Regulators cite a surge in scam activity as a primary driver of the restriction. Federal data from the FBI indicate that crypto‑ATM fraud has generated $389 million in losses, underscoring the risk profile for institutional exposure.

top_signals.title: Bitcoin Bulls Battle For Control With Emphasis On $80K Reclaim
top_signals.summary: Bitcoin is hovering just under $74,000 with a 0.98% gain. Market participants described as bulls are focusing on a reclaim of the $80,000 resistance level. Institutional investors are monitoring the price battle and bullish sentiment as an indicator of potential continued upward momentum.

top_signals.title: Bernstein Says IREN Pivot to AI Cloud Could Drive $3.7B Revenue
top_signals.summary: Bernstein analysts estimate that IREN’s AI cloud services could generate about $3.7 billion in revenue, positioning the segment as the company’s primary earnings source. The projection reflects a strategic pivot away from Bitcoin mining toward higher‑margin AI computing workloads. Bernstein raised its price target for IREN to $100, which translates to roughly a 100 percent upside from current levels. The firm notes that comparable mining companies are also reallocating capital to AI infrastructure, underscoring a broader industry transition.

top_signals.title: Banks are fighting a ‘sideshow’ as Clarity Act stalls. Will it matter?
top_signals.summary: The Senate Banking Committee has postponed the markup of the Clarity Act, a proposal intended to close a loophole that currently permits yield generation on stablecoins. The delay pushes formal debate on the measure into May, extending the period of regulatory uncertainty for banks and crypto firms. Pro‑stablecoin advocates characterize the banks’ resistance as a peripheral “sideshow” that will not alter the broader market trajectory. A White House analysis, however, estimates that any changes to bank lending resulting from the bill would be modest, suggesting limited immediate impact on institutional credit flows.

top_signals.title: Kbank Tests Ripple Wallet For Remittances In South Korea
top_signals.summary: South Korean internet‑only bank Kbank has formed a strategic partnership with Ripple to pilot blockchain‑based overseas remittances. The trial uses Ripple’s global network to test faster cheaper more transparent cross‑border payments to destinations such as the UAE and Thailand. The initiative comes as South Korea is considering stablecoin regulations, highlighting the potential for digital‑asset infrastructure in the region.

top_signals.title: 결제 시장 3.0: AI 에이전트 결제 시장 분석
top_signals.summary: The Tiger Research report identifies AI‑agent driven commerce as the next evolution of the payment market, creating demand for new transaction standards. It highlights a competitive race among technology firms to define those standards. Google is responding by developing the UCP and AP2 protocols, which combine product discovery with transaction authorization to secure future transaction‑based revenue. Institutional investors should watch how the adoption of these protocols could influence fee structures and market share in the emerging AI‑mediated payment ecosystem.

linkedin_post: Dear Founders, Investors, and Friends, The past weeks have reminded us how quickly the ecosystem can rally around risk and opportunity. After the April 18 exploit that drained over $290 million of rsETH from a LayerZero bridge, a coalition of Ethereum backers including Lido, EtherFi, Ethena, Mantle and Frax pledged 30,000 ETH to restore liquidity and protect providers. The coordinated response shows that deep capital pools can act as a safety net for DeFi when systemic stress appears. At the same time, Justin Sun has stepped forward with a $20 million USDT injection for Aave’s Core V3 market and a clear invitation for the protocol to launch on the Tron blockchain. Tron’s growing deposit base and Sun’s commitment illustrate the power of cross‑chain liquidity in attracting institutional users and expanding market depth. Finally, MicroStrategy’s latest purchase of 3,273 Bitcoin for roughly $255 million pushes its treasury past 818,000 BTC and keeps the company on track for the 1 million‑Bitcoin goal. This move reinforces the narrative that large corporates continue to view Bitcoin as a core store of value. For us at Blockwall, these developments reinforce the importance of backing resilient infrastructure, encouraging cross‑chain bridges and supporting long‑term treasury strategies. How do you see the next wave of capital allocation shaping the future of decentralized finance? #Web3 #Crypto #Blockchain #CryptoVC
